builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
summary: The method replaces costly manual reproduction and robustness checking of published statistical findings with LLM agents that execute analyses and systematically vary analytical choices. It costs API-level LLM spend plus engineering effort to build a domain-grounded benchmark (here, 20 SEER-based papers) and to curate executable baselines, with no large-scale training required. It can fail on the roughly 22% of claims not reproduced, on agents proposing indefensible alternative analyses, and by generating false-positive flags that consume expert review time.
rationale: The approach is domain-specific to SEER cancer-registry studies and validated on only 20 papers, so it is a relevant pattern for agent-assisted scientific review but not yet a general production tool for a typical ML engineering team.
technique: LLM agents for automated reproduction and robustness analysis

claims.statement: The method replaces costly manual reproduction and robustness checking of published statistical findings with LLM agents that execute analyses and systematically vary analytical choices. It costs API-level LLM spend plus engineering effort to build a domain-grounded benchmark (here, 20 SEER-based papers) and to curate executable baselines, with no large-scale training required. It can fail on the roughly 22% of claims not reproduced, on agents proposing indefensible alternative analyses, and by generating false-positive flags that consume expert review time.
The agent reproduces 77.4% of 2,190 atomic claims, and the robustness pipeline flags potentially consequential analytical choices in 9.5% of fully reproduced findings.
